# The shape of the glossary (fixture)

Each term is a block with two sentences an owner understands and the word the screen really uses for
it. The on-screen word is checked VERBATIM against the shipped console, so when the console renames
something this file is what fails, and the glossary row is what gets corrected.

### A bot
A helper with its own name, its own job and its own conversation. I am one of them and I run the
others for you.
- The word on your screen: Bots

### An agent
The same thing as a bot. Both words mean one helper, and the screen mostly says the first.
- The word on your screen: Workers

### A routine
A standing job you give me once and I do on a clock. They arrive switched off so nothing starts
behind your back.
- The word on your screen: Routines

### A playbook
Written instructions one of us follows when a job comes up. You can read them and change them.
- The word on your screen: Skills

### A workspace
Everything you signed into: your console, every bot on it, and the one computer they share. Nobody
else can see into it.
- The word on your screen: Machine Room

### The computer they share
One machine all your bots work on. Your files and logins stay on it between jobs.
- The word on your screen: Titan's computer

### An app you connect
Something you already pay for that we can reach, like your task list or your chat. You connect it
once and every bot here can use it.
- The word on your screen: Marketplace

### Where a credential goes
A private box on that app's own page. You type it there, it is kept away, and no bot ever sees it.
- The word on your screen: Accounts

### How I answer
The thinking your plan already pays for. You do not choose it per question.
- The word on your screen: How Titan answers

### A separate machine for code
A throwaway computer we borrow for real programming and give back. It has no way out to the web.
- The word on your screen: Files

### What wakes your phone
The short alerts you pick, and the devices that get them. Quiet hours are yours to set.
- The word on your screen: Notifications

### The web on my screen
A browser I drive myself, which you can watch and take the keyboard on at any time.
- The word on your screen: Desktop
